chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with them both) told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, who said: Al-Nadr ibn Shu'aib narrated to us from Abd al-Ghaffar al-Jazi, who said: The one who asked him (meaning al-Sadiq, peace be upon him) told me:

'Can there be disbelief that does not reach (the extent of) polytheism?' He said: 'Indeed, disbelief is polytheism.' Then he stood up and entered the mosque, and he turned to me and said: 'Yes, (that applies if) a man carries a narration to his companion, and so he does not teach him, and so he returns it to him. It is, then, a grace that he has rejected, and it does not reach polytheism.'

key_terms.كُفْر: Disbelief, rejection of truth or grace
key_terms.نِعْمَة: Grace, blessing, or favor (here referring to the hadith/knowledge)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between major polytheism and the minor disbelief of rejecting a grace?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between major polytheism (shirk) and a specific form of minor disbelief (kufr) where one rejects divine grace by failing to convey knowledge or a hadith to others. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly view that ingratitude for transmitted religious knowledge constitutes a form of rejection that falls short of full apostasy, emphasizing the communal responsibility of preserving and sharing the Imam's teachings.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, and Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they both said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja’far al-Himyari, from Muhammed bin Hussain bin Abi’l-Khattab, that he said: We were told by Nadr bin Shu’aib, from Abdul-Ghaffar al-Jazi, that he said: I was told by the one who asked him – meaning al-Sadiq, peace be upon him:

Can there be disbelief that does not reach (the extent of) polytheism? He said: Indeed, disbelief is polytheism. Then he stood up and entered the mosque, and he turned to me and said: Yes, (that applies if) a man carries a narration to his companions, and so he does not teach him, and so he returns it to him. It is, then, a grace that he has rejected, and it does not reach polytheism.
